corpus.name: OWASP GenAI Red Team Lab
corpus.note: Intentionally-vulnerable red-team lab. Intent does not remove a defect: a code-level security flaw is in ground truth whether or not it was planted on purpose.

method: Manual source review of every .py/.js/.cs file reachable from sandboxes/ and exploitation/. Each entry was confirmed by reading the source, the request-derived origin of the tainted value, and the sink. No scanner output was consulted while authoring this file.

scoping_rules.in_scope: Code-level security defects (CWE-mapped) with a demonstrable untrusted source and a dangerous sink, plus credentials that participate in an authorization decision.
scoping_rules.credential_positive: A string literal is a CWE-798 ground-truth positive iff some code path compares it against a request-derived value to grant or deny access, OR it is committed in configuration and posted as an authentication credential.
scoping_rules.credential_dedup: A client-side literal mirroring a separate enforcement-site literal of the same secret is not counted twice; the enforcement site is the positive.
scoping_rules.credential_negative: A literal handed to an SDK where the receiving side performs no authentication is a negative control, not a credential. Value entropy does not decide this - the presence of an authorization decision does.
scoping_rules.command_injection: shell=True / os.system with an f-string is a positive only when an untrusted value can reach it. A value derived from a fixed literal list, a constant, or a local operator menu is a negative control.

positives.title: Unsanitized path parameter written to disk
positives.why: object_key is joined into target_dir with os.path.join (line 32) with no basename(), no '..' rejection and no resolve()-based containment check, then opened for writing. bucket_name (line 27) is equally unsanitized, so an absolute or '..' bucket escapes data/ as well.

positives.title: Arbitrary file read from request body
positives.why: The 'peek:<path>' action passes the request-controlled remainder straight to _peek, which strips whitespace and opens it. No allow-list, no prefix check, no realpath containment.

positives.title: Arbitrary file write from request body
positives.why: The 'drop:<path>:<content>' action writes attacker-controlled content to an attacker-controlled path. The code even checks 'if "__init__.py" in path' (line 359) to confirm the write target is an importable package file - the RCE impact is acknowledged, the containment is absent.

positives.title: Traversal detected but not enforced
positives.why: is_traversal is computed at lines 289-291 and then only reported back to the caller as a string (line 311-313). The write at line 305 proceeds unconditionally. Detection without enforcement is still the vulnerability.

positives.source: request body data['query'] (line 190) -> regex capture of Action Input path (line 203) -> handle_document_reader(path) (line 206)
positives.title: Path from agent tool input read without validation
positives.why: target_path_str is parsed out of the request body with a regex and converted to a Path, then resolve()ed and opened. resolve() only normalises - it does not confine - so ../../../../etc/passwd reads normally. Reachable when LC_VERSION_TUPLE < (1,2,25), which is the version this sandbox pins at stage 0.

positives.title: Attacker-controlled Python written into an importable package
positives.why: payload is written into core/__init__.py inside a dataset that is then served over HTTP and pulled into site-packages/llama_index by download_dataset_and_source_files (lines 417-420). Direct request-body-to-code-execution.

positives.title: API key literal is the sole authorization check
positives.why: verify_api_key compares the bearer token against the literal sk-mock-key to grant or deny every /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings call. This is an authorization decision on a network-exposed surface, so it is a positive under the credential rule regardless of the value looking like a placeholder.

positives.title: Shared secret literal is the sole authorization check
positives.why: Same structure as GT-07: the literal 'foobar' is compared against the request header to authorize every object upload.

positives.title: Committed login password
positives.why: attack.py line 16 loads it and posts it to /rest/login (lines 73-82) to obtain the n8n-auth cookie. It is a working credential committed to source.

positives.title: Committed login password
positives.why: setup_target.py line 119 passes config['password'] to login(), which posts it to /rest/login (lines 21-25). Working credential committed to source.

positives.title: Committed API key used as X-API-KEY
positives.why: Used as the X-API-KEY header on /api/api_message (lines 39-40). It is the fallback when neither the flag nor the environment supplies one, so the key is live by default.

negative_controls.why_not_a_finding: engine is returned by detect_container_engine(), which iterates the fixed literal list ['docker', 'podman'] (line 165) and returns one of them. CONTAINER_NAME is the module constant 'haystack-sandbox' (line 34). No untrusted value can reach this call, so there is no injection. Reporting it means the rule fires on an f-string alone.
Identical construction to NC-01 with the same fixed-list engine and constant container name.
Generic CLI runner: cmd is a bare parameter of run_cmd(). No caller in this repository demonstrates an untrusted value reaching it, so the shell=True alone does not establish a vulnerability.
Dead assignment: verify_api_key() compares against the literal 'sk-mock-key' at line 43 and never reads this environment variable, so no authorization decision depends on it.

SDK constructor argument for a local Ollama endpoint. Ollama performs no API-key authentication, so nothing is authenticated by this literal. Also present in sandboxes/*/app/mocks/openai.py at the OpenAI(...) construction sites.

negative_controls.pattern: SELECT role, content FROM conversation_log WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?
negative_controls.why_not_a_finding: Fully parameterised query with placeholders; the same holds for every execute() in this file. There is no string-built SQL anywhere in it.
